behaviour: Artifactory accepts the Hugging Face upload calls that huggingface_hub makes: create repository, pre-upload check, Git LFS batch, object upload, commit, and a README metadata validation call (POST /api/validate-yaml).
source: https://docs.jfrog.com/artifactory/docs/use-hugging-face-with-jfrog-cli (wraps huggingface_hub upload_folder); the exact set of calls is read from the installed client
check: Run jf hf upload against the real instance and compare the calls it makes with the stand-in's call record; confirm /api/validate-yaml is answered.

behaviour: Names that break JFrog's naming rules are refused with HTTP 400 and a readable message naming the field.
source: JFrog documents the naming rules; the answer is not documented
check: Upload with an organisation starting with a hyphen and read the status and body.

behaviour: A repeat upload of a complete version without Delete/Overwrite permission is answered 409 at the commit call and changes nothing.
source: JFrog documents 409 for overwriting the same version without permission; the call that answers it is assumed to be the commit
check: Upload the same revision twice and see which call answers 409 and its body.

behaviour: A revision given as 40 hexadecimal characters is kept as the version's revision; a named revision (such as main) is mapped to a computed 40-character hash.
source: The design fetches at the commit hash; how Artifactory treats a given revision is not documented
check: Upload with revision set to a 40-character hash and fetch at that hash.

behaviour: A version becomes visible only when its commit succeeds; files received earlier are hidden and a stopped upload leaves it absent.
source: The design needs a repeat after a stop to find the version complete or absent
check: Stop an upload between the object upload and the commit and list the version.

behaviour: A checksum that does not match the uploaded content of a large object is refused with 422.
The large-object upload address carries a key in its query string instead of the token, because the client does not send the token there.
source: Git LFS upload addresses are usually pre-signed; Artifactory's form is not documented
check: Read the upload address Artifactory returns from the large-file batch call and what headers it needs.

behaviour: The storage-style listing GET /artifactory/api/storage/<repo>/<path>?list&deep=1 returns each file's uri, size and checksum (as sha2 and sha256).
source: Artifactory's File List API; the Machine Learning layout's paths are not documented
check: List a model version and read the paths and checksum field names.

behaviour: Two invented layouts stand in for the real one: flat (<org>/<model>/<revision>/<file>) and nested (<org>/<model>/revisions/<revision>/files/<file>).
source: The Machine Learning layout is not documented on the pages read (open item X1); JFrog's Hugging Face page only hints at <repo>/models/<org>/<model>/... and the gateway also tries that prefix
check: List a real version and record the real layout; the gateway must not depend on either invented one.

behaviour: Deleting a version is DELETE /artifactory/<repo>/<version folder> and answers 204; deleting a version that is not there answers 404.
source: Artifactory deletes artifacts and folders by path; the Machine Learning layout's version folder is not documented
check: Delete a version folder and read the status; delete it again.

behaviour: A token without write permission is answered 403 on every changing call; a wrong or missing token is answered 401.
A file path that is empty, absolute, contains '..' or a backslash is refused with 400.
An empty version (a commit with no files) is accepted and gives a complete version with no files; paths are compared exactly (case-sensitive).
Test-only answers: 404 not_imitated for any call the stand-in does not imitate, 501 content_not_kept for a file whose content was not kept, and 500 server_error for an imitated failure.
